messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a weird perf regression on the kvcache handoff tests overnight. latency p50 jumped ~2.3x for a subset of traces. NVTX shows a lot of tiny OSRT segments, looks like exec fragmentation. Has anyone seen sampling hide kernels here?

maya: Trying an nsys capture now but want flags that won't truncate the tail or bias sampling. Any capture recipes?

alex: Yep, short captures can bias sampling toward the busiest kernels and miss sporadic KV eviction work. For this kind of intermittent handoff you want: longer bracketed capture, osrt traces, and both cuda+nvtx. Also prefer sample-based profiling (cpu+gpu) to avoid huge trace files.

alex: Example I usually start with:

```bash
nsys profile --output=kv-handoff-2155 \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu,gpu \
  --capture-range=bracketed \
  --duration=12s \
  --force-overwrite
```

alex: Then post-process the sqlite with the timeline to find 1) tiny OSRT blocks 2) kernel selection churn around batching boundaries.

liam: Also try a two-pass strategy: 1) long, low-sample-rate capture to see the rare evictions (12-20s), 2) short dense capture when you see the hotspot to collect detailed kernel timelines (3-5s). For short runs use --sample-rate to increase samples per-second.

liam: Eg: `--sample-frequency=500` for short bursts (note that higher freq -> bigger files).

sarah: If you suspect the runtime is switching kernels (quantized vs fp32 fallback) add env logs and NVTX around kernel selection points in code. NVTX markers make it trivial to filter timeline windows. Also capture host stacks (cpu) to see scheduler delays: `--sample=cpu` is helpful.

sarah: Small tip: bracketed capture + `nsys stats --report=timeline` will show osrt slices aligned with NVTX pushes. If you see many 10-50us OSRT blocks, that's usually async small-dispatch noise or preemption.

maya: Good call — I'll add NVTX push/pop around kv_fetch/kv_evict and run the long capture first.

perf-bot: nightly-kv-handshake: p50=28.4ms (+130%), p95=121.7ms (+85%). Attached build: build-2026-03-17-rt-42.

alex: If the bracketed capture still misses the rare spike, try `--capture-range=nvtx` and put an NVTX marker around the suspected window from the test harness (gives exact start/stop). That avoids guesswork and keeps capture size small.

liam: Also check kernel selection code for fallthrough: when batch size == 1 we sometimes pick a 'scalar' kernel which is much slower. If you see kernel name flipping in timeline, that's the smoking gun.

maya: Awesome. Running the long capture now on dedicated node (g5x-large). Will paste sqlite and screenshots after export. Thanks 🙏 :thumbsup:
